children: A senior Treasury Department official who was forced out of his job this year is heading back to the private sector, joining the lobbying arm of accounting firm EY.

Kenneth Kies, who was assistant secretary for tax policy and acting chief counsel of the Internal Revenue Service, left the government after he warned that the White House was at risk of violating a federal law prohibiting senior officials' involvement in IRS audits, The Wall Street Journal reported in July.

Kies will be a senior adviser at Washington Council Ernst & Young, temporarily limited in his ability to contact his former Treasury and IRS colleagues. The firm's lobbying clients include MetLife, Citigroup and NextEra Energy, according to federal records.

Before joining the Trump administration, Kies ran his own tax lobbying firm. Earlier in his career, he was a House Republican tax aide and chief of staff of the nonpartisan congressional Joint Committee on Taxation.

"I am excited to join this talented team and help clients understand the evolving tax policy landscape, anticipate legislative and regulatory developments, and achieve their long-term objectives," he said.
